Does each hub's SKILL.md and README match what the v4.0.0.0 and v4.0.1.0 notes say it ships, including the sk-design consolidation and the Retired Surfaces section?

label: sk-doc leaf-manifest.json lists five sk-create-quality-control leaves as packet-local paths that do not exist; the files live under shared/ and ROUTER.md spells them with the shared/ alias, so manifest and router disagree about the same resources.

The v4.0.0.0 note names sk-code's three surfaces as sk-code-webflow, sk-code-skilled and sk-code-obsidian, but the v4.0.0.0 tag registry ships sk-code-webflow, sk-code-opencode and sk-code-obsidian; the note's middle name is the later rename.

sk-doc render-test fixture web-markup-and-css.md still carries seven links to sk-design-fundamentals, which v4.0.1.0 retired and sk-design v3.0.0.0 deleted; the links no longer resolve, and no script consumer of the fixture name was found.

sk-design is the only one of the four hubs with no README.md; sk-doc, sk-code and sk-prompt each ship one. The parent-hub companion-file policy requires a README per packet, not per hub root, so nothing breaks, but the hub root has no non-AI-facing overview.
All 15 sk-doc, 5 sk-code and 3 sk-design workflowMode entries resolve to <packet>/SKILL.md; sk-prompt has no mode registry and all 35 of its manifest leaves resolve.
Current hub counts match their registries: sk-doc 15 modes across 14 packets and 13 /create:* commands; sk-code 3 surfaces; sk-design 3 modes after the v4.0.1.0 retirement.

sk-prompt is a standalone skill with no mode-registry.json or hub-router.json; its leaf-manifest still carries one modes entry, which is not a canon violation because the companion-file policy applies to parent hubs.
Every workflowMode in a hub mode-registry.json must resolve to <packet>/SKILL.md.
Every leaf in leaf-manifest.json must resolve on disk either packet-relative or through its authored shared/ alias.

direction: Treating sk-prompt's missing mode-registry.json and hub-router.json as a canon violation
reason: sk-prompt is a standalone skill, not a parent hub; the companion-file policy requires those files only for hubs.
